summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 with 7 compressed rotations via copytruncate, so the writing application never loses its open file descriptor across rotation. Validated config syntax, proved rotation continuity empirically with a live simulated writer process, proved the 7-rotation retention cap by forcing 9 cycles, confirmed the logrotate.timer drives daily execution, restored a clean baseline, and completed the mandatory restart protocol on node1 with proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: found /var/log/inventory/app.log with no backing service process (static log file scenario); confirmed logrotate binary present
Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with: daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Validated config syntax and scheduling logic with logrotate -d
Ran a background writer process continuously appending to app.log to simulate a live application holding an open file descriptor

Forced a rotation while the writer was active: app.log truncated to 0, a rotated copy created, writer process kept running uninterrupted, and new writes correctly landed in the fresh app.log while prior content was preserved in the rotated file
Removed dateext from initial config after discovering it caused same-day forced-rotation filename collisions; switched to standard numbered rotation (.1, .2.gz, ...) for unambiguous behavior
Forced 9 sequential rotation cycles and confirmed exactly 7 rotations retained (.1 uncompressed per delaycompress, .2.gz-.7.gz compressed), oldest pruned beyond 7
Confirmed logrotate.timer is enabled/active and scheduled to fire daily at 00:00, providing the daily cadence
Cleaned up all test artifacts and restored app.log to a clean baseline state
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, config presence, timer status, log health
Triggered a background-delayed systemctl reboot on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed (513c865e... -> 11ea8768...), confirming an actual reboot occurred

Verified post-restart recovery: logrotate config file intact, logrotate.timer active with correct next-fire schedule, app.log present and correctly formed, logrotate -d confirms rotation policy still valid

evidence.summary: logrotate.d config written with 'daily' directive, syntax validated via logrotate -d, and logrotate.timer confirmed enabled/active/scheduled for daily midnight execution

Config reset with rotate 7/compress/delaycompress; 9 forced rotation cycles produced exactly 7 retained rotations (app.log.1 through app.log.7.gz), with the oldest pruned, and compression applied to all but the most recent (delaycompress)

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A live writer process (PID 1569) was appending continuously; after a forced rotation the process remained alive and unaffected, old content was preserved in the rotated file, and new writes correctly appeared in the fresh app.log, proving copytruncate preserves write continuity without needing a signal/restart
Captured boot_id 513c865e-e121-4025-a0a4-8689cc580398, confirmed logrotate.d config present, logrotate.timer active, and app.log intact before reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded a delayed systemctl reboot; the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 restart disconnection and recovery of connectivity
evidence.summary: Poll attempt during reboot returned a connection timeout (node down); subsequent poll succeeded, confirming the node came back online

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 11ea8768-f1c1-4749-a060-b02fcc7bd171 differs from the pre-restart boot_id 513c865e-e121-4025-a0a4-8689cc580398, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of rotation config and log health
evidence.summary: After restart, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app config persisted unchanged, logrotate.timer is active with correct next-fire time, app.log is intact with expected content, and logrotate -d confirms the rotation policy is still valid
